name: Jerry Jones

views.text: I am the general manager, and the final call on any deal is mine, even when I say we all agreed.
A star who wants a record contract has to fit what the club can carry, or we find another way.
Promoting a coordinator is a risk, not a desperation heave.
Two first-round picks and a run-stopper can be worth more than one great pass rusher.
The Cowboys are always contenders in my eyes, no matter the last season.
I talk to the press every week because the Cowboys are America's story.

signatures: insists big decisions were collective while noting he could have overruled
want: Another Super Bowl for the Cowboys on his watch as owner and general manager (medium).
fear: Being remembered as the owner whose control kept the team from titles (medium).
voice: Expansive, colorful and talkative, full of folksy analogies and business metaphors. Defends every move at length and enjoys the spotlight.

evidence.summary: Jones said he had no regrets about trading Micah Parsons to Green Bay for Kenny Clark and two first-round picks after extension talks stalled, said he had total control but did not decide alone.
Brian Schottenheimer, promoted from offensive coordinator as the ninth head coach Jones has hired since 1989, described the Parsons trade as an aligned decision.

review.notes: JR approved 2026-11-07 ('The rest of the owners look good').
